kind: K6 Ek K draft (Claude + gpt-6.1-sol medium decision, 4 Oct 2026)
question: Mobil robotların engelden kaçınan yörünge planlamasında model öngörülü kontrol nasıl formüle edilmiştir? Dinamik modeli, karar değişkenlerini, amaç fonksiyonunu, engel ve hareket kısıtlarını ve değerlendirme koşullarını karşılaştırın.

claims.claim_statement: Integrating a control barrier function into a Lyapunov-based stabilizing MPC for a differential-drive mobile robot yields both closed-loop stability and safety among static and moving obstacles.

elements.text: A stabilizing MPC built with Lyapunov stability theory on the robot's kinematic model
A control barrier function constraint integrated into that MPC
Both stability and safety are obtained for the closed loop
The workspace contains static and moving obstacles

conditions: differential-drive wheeled mobile robot with non-holonomic kinematics
claims.nearest_simple_explanation: A plain MPC with a distance-based collision penalty already avoids obstacles without any barrier function.
claims.critical_assumption: The barrier constraint stays feasible together with the Lyapunov-based stabilizing terms at every step.
claims.validation_plan: Find a report that combines a Lyapunov-based stabilizing MPC with a CBF for a differential-drive robot and states stability and safety with moving obstacles.

N.title: Model Predictive Control with Safety Guarantee for Moving Obstacle Avoidance of Mobile Robots
Dynamic Control Barrier Function-based Model Predictive Control to Safety-Critical Obstacle-Avoidance of Mobile Robot

claims.claim_statement: Supplying deep-learning multimodal predictions of dynamic-obstacle positions to a nonlinear MPC enables collision-free trajectory tracking for a mobile robot and outperforms non-deep-learning methods in complex scenarios.

elements.text: Deep-learning multimodal prediction of several plausible future positions of dynamic obstacles
The predictions are used by a nonlinear MPC solver
Collision-free trajectory tracking is achieved
The approach outperforms non-deep-learning methods
Complex scenarios with stochastic dynamic obstacles

claims.nearest_simple_explanation: A constant-velocity obstacle prediction inside the same MPC already avoids most dynamic obstacles.
claims.critical_assumption: The learned predictor generalizes to the obstacle motion seen at run time.
claims.validation_plan: Find a report that couples a learned multimodal obstacle predictor to an NMPC and compares it with non-learning predictors.

N.title: Prescient Collision-Free Navigation of Mobile Robots With Iterative Multimodal Motion Prediction of Dynamic Obstacles
Motion Prediction Based on Multiple Futures for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance of Mobile Robots

claims.claim_statement: A scenario-tree prediction of dynamic-obstacle trajectories in a multi-stage NMPC avoids collisions with dynamic obstacles, is less conservative than a nominal NMPC with the predicted scenarios added as constraints, costs more computation, and both strategies run in real time.

elements.text: Scenario-tree prediction of the dynamic obstacle's trajectories
Multi-stage NMPC with recourse in the robot's predicted controls
Less conservative than nominal NMPC with scenario constraints
Higher computational effort than the nominal strategy
Both strategies are applicable in real time

claims.nearest_simple_explanation: Adding one worst-case obstacle prediction as a constraint to a nominal NMPC is enough.
claims.critical_assumption: The scenario set covers the obstacle's actual motion.
claims.validation_plan: Find a report that compares multi-stage scenario-tree NMPC with nominal NMPC with scenario constraints for mobile robots.

N.title: Robust NMPC Schemes for the Control of Mobile Robots in the Presence of Dynamic Obstacles

claims.claim_statement: A nonlinear MPC for a mobile robot with a SINDy-identified prediction model and a control barrier function safety constraint is input-to-state stable with respect to the prediction error and solves within a 10 ms control period on a Husky A200.

elements.text: Prediction model identified from noisy data with sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics
Control barrier function safety constraint inside the NMPC
Input-to-state stability with respect to the prediction error
Solve time within a 10 ms control period
Tests on a Husky A200 robot

claims.nearest_simple_explanation: A first-principles kinematic model with the same constraint would behave identically.
claims.critical_assumption: The identified model's error stays bounded during operation.
claims.validation_plan: Find a report with SINDy-based NMPC plus CBF, an ISS result, and a reported per-step solve time.

N.title: Model-Free Safety Critical Model Predictive Control for Mobile Robot in Dynamic Environments

claims.claim_statement: A priority-based distributed MPC that orders networked differential-drive robots by urgency and solves non-convex collision constraints by sequential convex programming avoids collisions without losing prediction consistency, validated on at least 10 physical robots.

elements.text: Priority queue by an urgency value, converted to a topological order
Sequential convex programming of the non-convex collision constraints
Collision avoidance without loss of prediction consistency
Validation on at least 10 physical robots

claims.nearest_simple_explanation: Fixed-priority distributed MPC already prevents collisions.
claims.critical_assumption: Communication delays are small compared with the sampling period.
claims.validation_plan: Find a report of urgency-ordered distributed MPC with SCP and physical-robot validation with robot counts.

N.title: Distributed Non-Convex Model Predictive Control for Non-Cooperative Collision Avoidance of Networked Differential Drive Mobile Robots

claims.claim_statement: An MPC for a differential-drive robot that builds obstacle constraints from the signed distance field of an occupancy map and adapts its horizon online from the measured closing speed to the nearest obstacle keeps at least 0.3 m clearance and cuts mean solve time by at least 30% against a fixed horizon.

elements.text: Obstacle constraints taken from a signed distance field of an occupancy map
Horizon length adapted online from the measured closing speed to the nearest obstacle
Minimum clearance of at least 0.3 m is kept
Mean solve time is at least 30% lower than with a fixed horizon

conditions: differential-drive robot with an occupancy map
claims.nearest_simple_explanation: A shorter fixed horizon gives the same solve-time saving.
claims.critical_assumption: The adapted horizon never becomes too short to see an approaching obstacle.
claims.validation_plan: Find a report with SDF obstacle constraints and an online-adapted horizon with clearance and solve-time numbers.
